summary: Users import mountainash-utils-files to read, write, list, delete, copy, and transform files across local disk, S3-family, Azure, GCS, SFTP, FTP, SMB, HTTP/S, and GitHub. They interact primarily with StorageFacade, read_bytes(), copy_between(), the transform pipeline, and provider settings classes.

concepts.name: Reading and writing files
recommended_docs: facade.read(path), facade.read_stream(path), facade.write(path, data), facade.write_stream(path, stream)

concepts.name: Listing, deleting, copying
recommended_docs: list_files(prefix), list_directories(prefix), delete(path), copy(source, dest), exists(path), metadata(path)

concepts.name: Cross-backend file transfer
recommended_docs: copy_between(src_facade, src_path, dst_facade, dst_path, source_pipeline=None, destination_pipeline=None)

concepts.name: Compression and encryption pipelines
recommended_docs: Pipeline(Gzip(), GPG(recipients=[...])), read(path, pipeline=p), write(path, data, pipeline=p). Outermost transform listed first.

concepts.name: Suffix-inferred pipelines
recommended_docs: read(path, infer=True) or read_bytes(path, infer=True) — .gz → Gzip, .gpg → GPG. Supply gpg= when GPG suffix is present.

concepts.name: Buffering a stream (materialize)
recommended_docs: materialize(stream, to='bytes') when downstream code needs a sized or seekable buffer

concepts.name: Handling errors
recommended_docs: Catch PathNotFoundError for missing files, UnsupportedOperationError for unimplemented ops, StorageConnectionError for connection failures, TransformError for pipeline failures

documentation_plan: Quick-start guide: read_bytes one-liner → StorageFacade → providers
Provider configuration reference per provider class (FLAVOR/SERVICE_TYPE tables)
Pipeline tutorial: Gzip, GPG, outermost-first semantics, infer=True
Error handling reference: which exception for which scenario
copy_between guide: cross-backend transfer with transform pipelines
materialize() guide: when and why to buffer
open_questions: Should read_bytes support auth_params for authenticated backends?
Should Pipeline ordering (outermost-first) be surfaced in a dedicated guide with visual diagrams?
GitHub backend is read-only — should this be more prominent in the provider docs?
